prompt: This code is supposed to use polymorphism but always prints 'Animal'. Why?
choices: Dog must implement name() from Animal
Static methods are class-level and not polymorphic — the declared reference type (Animal) determines which name() runs
a must be cast to Dog to use polymorphism
explanation: Static methods use static dispatch (method hiding, not overriding). a.name() resolves to Animal.name() because a is declared as Animal. To use polymorphism, make name() an instance method (non-static) and override it.
